messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT group PREFILL_OOM_HIGH_RATE — multiple CUDA OOMs during prefill. Pods restarting on cluster infer-prod-us-west-2. Detection window: 5m.

Maya (oncall): taking the page. seeing restart spikes on nodes auw-gn-2 and auw-gn-3. Affected pods are 'serving-runtime' containers running model xlarge-ctx. Symptoms: 500s returned to clients, latency spikes. Root logs show OOM during prefill.

Maya (oncall): recent container log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:34.521Z runtime ERROR cuda runtime: out of memory
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File \'/srv/runtime/prefill.py\', line 312, in do_prefill
      kv = allocate_kv_cache(batch, seq_len)
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.1 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 12.48 GiB already allocated)
  context: prefill seq_len=16384 batch=1 model_variant=xlarge-ctx
```

Carlos (runtime): confirmed. The prefill path allocates KV proportional to seq_len * num_attention_heads * head_dim. At seq_len ~16k we exceed typical 16GB GPUs when combined with batch and other allocations. We also saw a recent uptick in long-context traffic (customers sending very long prompts). Autoscaler did not add high-memory nodes because the emergency pool was at its max.

Priya (ml-infra): immediate mitigations we can try now:
- apply a temporary admission control to cap prefill tokens per request to 8k
- reduce prefill concurrency on runtime nodes to 1 or 2 to limit aggregate mem pressure
- spin up a high-mem node pool and route large-context requests there

Commands I propose for quick action (will run with ops creds):
```sh
# set runtime flags via internal API (no creds printed here)
curl -X POST 'https://console-api.internal/v1/flags' -d '{\'PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS\': 8192, \'PREFILL_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT\': 2}'

# cordon and label a node to accept highmem workload (example)
kubectl label node node-123 prefilling=highmem --overwrite

# create emergency nodepool (cloud CLI pseudo)
cloudctl nodepool create --name=emergency-highmem --machine-type=a100-40g --min=1 --max=4 --labels=prefilling=highmem
```

Carlos (runtime): on runtime side I will: 1) push a small config to reduce default prefill concurrency and enforce a per-request seq_len cap, 2) add a short-circuit to free KV allocation if seq_len estimate > 12k and return 413 with guidance. Pushing a canary now to 10% of traffic.

deploy-bot: starting canary deploy for serving-runtime flags (canary 10%).

Ben (support): opened ticket INC-4512 and notified affected customers. Customers report failures when sending large system prompts and concatenated logs. Asking whether we can offer a temporary fallback/older-model that does streaming prefill on CPU.

Maya (oncall): live mitigation plan (actions completed / in progress):
1) Applied PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=8192 via feature flag (in progress).
2) Reduced PREFILL_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT to 2 on suspect nodes (in progress).
3) Created emergency-highmem nodepool request to infra (requested).
4) Added ingress size check to reject requests > 256kB (PR open, will merge if canary stable).
5) Notified support to update customer-facing guidance: split prompts or use compressed embeddings.

Carlos (runtime): after reducing concurrency and applying token cap, we see immediate reduction in OOM errors. Metrics: OOM rate down ~80% in first 3m on canary. Affected pods still restarting occasionally on older nodes; will cordon those nodes as Priya requested.

Priya (ml-infra): cordoning node auw-gn-3 now to prevent noisy restarts. draining pods to other nodes labeled prefilling=highmem.
```sh
kubectl cordon auw-gn-3
kubectl drain auw-gn-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Maya (oncall): Monitoring dashboard link: https://monitoring.internal/redwood/incidents/1938456123 — OOM count chart and restart count. Will watch the 30m window.

Ben (support): updated INC-4512 customers with mitigation steps and ETA for full fix. Asking product if we can temporarily downgrade model variant for those tenants to medium-ctx to keep them online.

Carlos (runtime): we can add routing rule to move specific customer tokens to medium-ctx variant. Workaround implemented for 2 customers so far.

deploy-bot: canary progressed to 50% after 6m, no regressions observed.

Maya (oncall): Current status: OOM spikes reduced, some pods still flapping on older nodes that will be drained. Priority actions for next 8h: finish highmem nodepool provisioning, migrate heavy tenants, and add long-term runtime guardrails (auto-eviction for excessive prefill, better admission controls).

Priya (ml-infra): follow-up items assigned to infra backlog: increase emergency pool quotas, add autoscaler rule to prefer highmem machines for scheduling large seq_len pods, and document required labels.

Maya (oncall): Handoff: Priya owns infra follow-up & ticketing, Carlos owns runtime changes for graceful prefill failure mode and canary rollback plan. I'll continue monitoring until next on-call. If anyone sees 5xx spikes > 5% re-alert in channel.

Maya (oncall): :white_check_mark: closing page for immediate incident. Will re-open if OOM rate increases.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated (monitoring).
